hyperedges.label: Payment-before-KOT enforcement chain
hyperedges.description: No single pair captures it: the payments check constraint, the activation trigger, the ticket-insert trigger and the release path together guarantee that unverified money never reaches the kitchen.

hyperedges.label: Cross-boundary idempotency mesh
hyperedges.description: Seven independent unique keys spanning four migrations implement one invariant: any retry, webhook replay or concurrent confirmation produces exactly one activation, one grant, one order and one ticket.

hyperedges.label: Authorization-as-data resolution path
hyperedges.description: Every RLS policy and every KOT move resolves through the same chain of rows and helpers, which is why 'Owner may watch but not touch the KOT' is a data fact rather than a code branch.

hyperedges.label: Scheduled delivery released into a live kitchen ticket
Catalog edit propagating to the storefront
Payment verification and activation chain
hyperedges.rationale: Every route into activation passes the same four gates in order: session, payment ownership against customers.profile_id, gateway signature verification in confirmCheckout, then confirm_subscription_payment in the database. Only an 'active' outcome clears the draft. The sandbox route joins the chain at the same point a real gateway would, which is what makes it an end-to-end proof that an unverified or declined outcome creates no subscription and no KOT and that retries are idempotent.

hyperedges.label: KOT transition authorization chain
hyperedges.rationale: Both KOT write endpoints validate only the request shape, then call an RPC with the caller's own token. Legality of the move and the actor's permission (data in role_permissions) are decided by the database trigger, so an Owner's read-only KOT survives a direct API call and 'insufficient privilege' surfaces as 403.

hyperedges.label: Scheduled job layer
hyperedges.rationale: Three cron endpoints share one shape: bearer-secret authentication (no session exists), the service-role client, idempotent work, and GET aliased to POST for hosted schedulers. Each is isolated so a failure degrades one concern only -- a notification provider outage blocks no order, and a failing marketplace does not stop the other being reconciled.

hyperedges.label: Marketplace webhook ingestion path
hyperedges.note: One inbound request traverses all six: raw body read, signature verified (rejections logged to integration_events), idempotent ingestion into a KOT ticket, and on failure a provider-scoped breaker trip.

hyperedges.label: Payment confirmation and activation path
hyperedges.note: Checkout prices server-side and creates the payment; the webhook dedupes on the provider event id, matches the internal payment, and confirms it exactly once regardless of whether the browser callback also arrived.

hyperedges.label: Sign-in journey
hyperedges.note: Page redirects the already-authenticated by role, panel owns the credential state the demo table fills, form authenticates without revealing which emails exist, and the forbidden screen closes the loop by offering sign-out as the way back for a wrong-role session.

hyperedges.label: The shared button family
hyperedges.rationale: One class builder feeds three renderings that differ only in semantics: Button (does something, knows about a pending form via useFormStatus), ButtonLink (goes somewhere, a real <a> so tab order and open-in-new-tab work), ConfirmButton (does something destructive, composing Button twice to get arm-then-confirm). Spinner is the shared in-flight affordance for all of them.

hyperedges.label: Realtime KOT board sync and honesty
hyperedges.rationale: Both boards subscribe through useKotBoard and mutate through useTicketActions; ConnectionBadge exposes the subscription's real state so a silently stalled board is never mistaken for a live one, and TicketItems fetches lines per ticket so the realtime firehose stays cheap. The kitchen sees a money-free, large-type subset of the same ticket stream the manager acts on.

hyperedges.label: Idempotent, verified checkout
hyperedges.rationale: One key minted at configuration time travels in the draft cookie into begin_subscription_checkout, which replays instead of duplicating; the service then reuses any existing gateway order for that payment. Nothing is granted until confirmCheckout gets a verified signature, and the UI turns the three server outcomes into three honest screens including the unconfirmed one.

hyperedges.label: One PaymentAdapter contract, three gateways, one resolver
hyperedges.rationale: All three adapters absorb their gateway's idiosyncrasies (paise vs rupees, order id vs session token, HMAC vs re-query) so checkout code is identical, and all three obey the same two rules: verify on the server, never mutate application state. paymentAdapter() refuses an unconfigured adapter and configuredPaymentProviders() decides what is even offered, so a customer can never begin a checkout against a gateway that would fail.

hyperedges.label: Constant-time HMAC verification across every trust boundary
hyperedges.rationale: Every inbound trust boundary -- payment webhook, payment callback, marketplace webhook, cron header -- uses the same shape: recompute an HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW body (parsing first would break the signature), length-check, then timingSafeEqual. The signed material and encoding differ per provider (order|payment hex for Razorpay and sandbox, raw body hex for Razorpay webhooks and the marketplaces, timestamp+body base64 for Cashfree), but a missing secret or header is always a rejection, never a pass-through.

hyperedges.label: Realtime as signal: refetch, resync, and the DB wiring that backs it
hyperedges.rationale: The board never trusts a change payload as data -- only as a row id to refetch from v_kot_tickets -- which makes duplicate and out-of-order events idempotent and keeps the view's money-masking in force. Gaps are closed by full resync on reconnect, network-online and tab-visible, never by an interval. The anon browser client means RLS filters which events arrive at all, and the realtime test asserts the publication and the single SELECT policy that make both properties true at the database.

hyperedges.label: The Four-Role RBAC Model
hyperedges.rationale: Four staff roles whose boundaries are defined as role_permissions rows rather than code, each role's screen shaped by what it may not see: Owner watches without touching, Manager runs the floor without pricing, Kitchen cooks without money, Developer Admin configures everything but cannot rewrite history.

hyperedges.label: The Payment Safety Guarantee
hyperedges.rationale: Together these mean no food is cooked and no entitlement granted without a server-verified payment, retries cannot double-charge, uncertain outcomes are reconciled rather than guessed, and a fake gateway is unreachable in production.

hyperedges.label: The Honest-State Doctrine
hyperedges.rationale: One idea expressed at every layer: never display, imply or persist a state the system has not actually reached — no optimistic lies, no invented endpoints, no unvalidated number passing as decided, no silently swallowed refusal.

nodes.label: app_role (enum)
nodes.rationale: Roles are a closed kind-list; how MANY people hold a role is data in employees, never hardcoded (PRD 5).

nodes.label: order_source (enum)
nodes.rationale: SW=Swiggy, ZM=Zomato, SX=subscription. Every channel converges on one internal KOT; only the prefix differs.

nodes.label: kot_status (enum)
nodes.rationale: Kitchen lifecycle NEW->...->COMPLETED; REJECTED/CANCELLED are terminal side-exits, not happy-path states.

nodes.label: order_status (enum)
nodes.rationale: Order state is deliberately separate from payment state and KOT state - three machines that never write each other's columns (PRD 8, 20).

nodes.label: payment_provider (enum)
nodes.rationale: COD exists in the model but is paused; enabling it is a settings change, not a code change (PRD 3, 8).

nodes.label: subscription_status (enum)
nodes.rationale: pending_payment creates NO KOT; only a verified payment moves a subscription to active.

nodes.label: plan_type (enum)
nodes.rationale: Four plan shapes, none privileged in code: fixed_meals, meal_credits, scheduled_meals, customer_selected (PRD 7).

nodes.label: subscription_delivery_status (enum)
nodes.rationale: A scheduled delivery becomes operational only when released inside the KOT lead time.

nodes.label: credit_entry_type (enum)
nodes.rationale: Ledger is append-only: a reversal is a new compensating entry type, never an edit (PRD 7).

nodes.label: integration_capability_state (enum)
nodes.rationale: integrated|mocked|blocked - every marketplace feature is labelled so the UI never implies more than the API offers (PRD 16, 23).

nodes.label: auth_profiles (table)
nodes.rationale: One row per authenticated principal. Deletion disables login but preserves historical business records (PRD 14) - never a hard delete.

nodes.label: permissions (table)
nodes.rationale: Permission catalogue; codes are '<domain>.<action>' and are referenced by RLS policies AND the kot_transitions state machine.

nodes.label: role_permissions (table)
nodes.rationale: Authorization is data, not code: permissions can be retuned without a deploy (PRD 20).

nodes.label: employees (table)
nodes.rationale: Staffing counts are configurable rows, never constants - a fourth kitchen hand is an INSERT (PRD 5).

nodes.label: audit_logs (table)
nodes.rationale: Append-only; nobody including Owner may rewrite history. A trigger, not a RULE, because rules discard writes silently and block INSERT..ON CONFLICT (PRD 17).

nodes.label: app.current_actor_id()
nodes.rationale: Server jobs run as service_role with no JWT; they announce the real actor via the app.actor_id GUC so audit never says 'system'.

nodes.label: app.current_role()
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER so reading the caller's role inside an RLS policy does not re-enter RLS on auth_profiles (infinite recursion). search_path pinned to defeat hijacking.

nodes.label: app.is_direct_connection()
nodes.rationale: No PostgREST context = a migration/seed/psql session, already fully trusted; exempting it is what lets the bootstrap grant the first administrator their role.

nodes.label: app.has_permission(text)
nodes.rationale: The single authorization predicate every policy and the KOT trigger resolve through.

nodes.label: app.is_admin()
nodes.rationale: Owner and Developer Admin are the only audit-log readers (PRD 17).

nodes.label: app.forbid_mutation()
nodes.rationale: Generic append-only enforcement; raises insufficient_privilege on UPDATE/DELETE.

nodes.label: app.audit_trigger()
nodes.rationale: Records only keys that actually changed, and redacts a caller-supplied column list so secrets/PII never reach the trail. A no-op update writes no row.

nodes.label: public.record_audit_event()
nodes.rationale: Wrapper for non-row-shaped audit events (logins, config changes, state transitions).

nodes.label: audit_logs_append_only (trigger)
nodes.rationale: Blocks UPDATE/DELETE on the audit log so history is immutable even for the Owner.

nodes.label: business_settings (table)
nodes.rationale: Typed key/value store; nothing business-critical is a constant in application code. is_sensitive hides keys from Branch Manager/Kitchen; is_provisional marks values the Owner has not confirmed (PRD 20, 22).

nodes.label: delivery_settings (table)
nodes.rationale: Row-per-rule so fee tiers can be added without touching pricing code; highest-priority match wins.

nodes.label: tax_settings (table)
nodes.rationale: Two rows (CGST/SGST) so real GST treatment is a data change. Nothing in code assumes two components or 5% (PRD 6).

nodes.label: cost_settings (table)
nodes.rationale: Fee/cost assumptions behind estimated profit, explicitly flagged is_dummy_data. NULLS NOT DISTINCT unique index keeps the all-channels fallback row singular (PRD 12).

nodes.label: delivery_windows (table)
nodes.rationale: Breakfast/lunch/dinner are configurable rows, not an enum; each carries its own ordering cut-off (PRD 7).

nodes.label: app.setting_numeric(text)
nodes.rationale: A missing key fails loudly with no_data_found instead of silently defaulting to zero.

nodes.label: app.business_timezone()
nodes.rationale: Timezone is a setting, so a second branch in another zone needs no code change.

nodes.label: app.business_date(timestamptz)
nodes.rationale: Daily KOT sequences reset on the business-day boundary, not UTC midnight (PRD 10).

nodes.label: app.resolve_delivery_fee()
nodes.rationale: Pricing code calls this so a fee change is a row edit; explicit-source rules outrank the catch-all.

nodes.label: app.resolve_tax_components()
nodes.rationale: Returns one row per active component so invoices show the CGST/SGST split rather than one opaque tax line.

nodes.label: products (table)
nodes.rationale: Availability and visibility are separate: a hidden product disappears, an unavailable one renders grayscale but cannot be ordered. archived_at is a soft delete so historical order lines stay meaningful (PRD 13, 17, 19).

nodes.label: product_images (table)
nodes.rationale: Partial unique index guarantees at most one primary image per product.

nodes.label: variant_groups (table)
nodes.rationale: Defined once and attached to many products so 'Portion' is not re-created per meal.

nodes.label: variants (table)
nodes.rationale: credit_delta exists because a larger portion can legitimately cost an extra credit.

nodes.label: product_variant_groups (table)
nodes.rationale: is_required_override lets one product make a normally optional group required.

nodes.label: app.product_is_orderable()
nodes.rationale: Both API and RLS use this, so 'unavailable products cannot be selected' is never only a frontend concern (PRD 6, 19).

nodes.label: customers (table)
nodes.rationale: profile_id is nullable so the Owner can create a customer who has never signed in. Marketing consent is deliberately independent of account status: deleting an account is not permission to keep marketing (PRD 14).

nodes.label: customer_addresses (table)
nodes.rationale: Partial unique index enforces one default address per active customer.

nodes.label: app.current_customer_id()
nodes.rationale: Customer-facing RLS compares against this rather than trusting any client-supplied customer_id.

nodes.label: customers_audit (trigger, redacts email/phone)
nodes.rationale: Keeps the change history but redacts contact PII the log does not need to prove who changed what.

nodes.label: customer_addresses_audit (trigger, redacts address PII)
nodes.rationale: Redacts phone, address lines, landmark and coordinates from the audit trail.

nodes.label: subscription_plans (table)
nodes.rationale: Check constraint forces each plan shape to carry the entitlement it is meaningless without. Plan-level nulls mean 'use the global setting', so defaults live in exactly one place (PRD 7).

nodes.label: subscription_plan_meals (table)
nodes.rationale: Serves fixed/scheduled plans (the meals) and customer_selected plans (the is_selectable pool) from one table.

nodes.label: subscriptions (table)
nodes.rationale: Created pending_payment; plan_snapshot freezes commercial terms so editing a plan later never restates what an existing customer bought. grace_period_days is frozen at purchase so a settings change cannot retroactively expire someone.

nodes.label: subscription_credit_ledger (table)
nodes.rationale: Append-only ledger, not a mutable balance (PRD 7). Balance is always sum(credits); (subscription_id, idempotency_key) unique makes retried credit operations non-double-charging.

nodes.label: subscription_deliveries (table)
nodes.rationale: Unique (subscription_id, scheduled_date, delivery_window_id) is what makes the schedule generator idempotent - a re-run collides instead of duplicating.

nodes.label: subscription_pauses (table)
nodes.rationale: An explicit history rather than a mutable 'paused' flag, so pause quotas can be counted and audited (PRD 7).

nodes.label: public.subscription_credit_balance()
nodes.rationale: Balance is always derived from the ledger, never cached in a column.

nodes.label: subscription_credit_ledger_append_only (trigger)
nodes.rationale: A correction is a new compensating entry, never an edit - which is the whole point of a ledger.

nodes.label: orders (table)
nodes.rationale: Check constraints enforce channel shape: an SX order needs a real subscription delivery; a marketplace order needs an external_order_id. Address/name snapshots mean a later profile edit cannot rewrite what was delivered (PRD 17).

nodes.label: order_items (table)
nodes.rationale: Name and price are snapshotted: renaming or repricing a product must not alter a historical ticket or invoice.

nodes.label: kot_daily_counters (table)
nodes.rationale: Counter row locked per (business_date, source) via INSERT..ON CONFLICT so concurrent inserts cannot collide.

nodes.label: kot_tickets (table)
nodes.rationale: One ticket per order. Original prep ETA is preserved beside the override so a manager change is visible rather than silent. Rejection must always carry a reason (PRD 9).

nodes.label: kot_transitions (table)
nodes.rationale: The KOT state machine as DATA: which moves exist and which permission each needs are rows. This is what makes 'Owner KOT is read-only' enforceable server-side without a code branch per role.

nodes.label: order_number_seq (sequence)
nodes.rationale: A single sequence across all sources, 1..99,999,999; distinct from the daily source-prefixed KOT number (PRD 10).

nodes.label: app.next_kot_daily_number()
nodes.rationale: SW-001/ZM-001/SX-001, reset every business day.

nodes.label: app.kot_enforce_transition()
nodes.rationale: Rejects illegal transitions AND unauthorised actors, stamps the lifecycle timestamp, and writes the status event - so history cannot be skipped by a client that forgets to write it.

nodes.label: app.kot_record_creation()
nodes.rationale: Records the ticket's birth as an event so the history has no gap.

nodes.label: app.order_record_transition()
nodes.rationale: Orders move under server control only, and every move leaves an event.

nodes.label: kot_tickets_enforce_transition (trigger)
nodes.rationale: BEFORE UPDATE OF status - the single choke point every KOT move passes through.

nodes.label: idempotency_keys (table)
nodes.rationale: Generic API idempotency store: any financial or order-creating endpoint records its key first, so a retry replays the stored response instead of doing the work twice (PRD 7, 11).

nodes.label: payments (table)
nodes.rationale: payments_target check: a payment pays for exactly one of an order or a subscription. payments_success_is_verified check: status 'success' is impossible without verified_at, and the browser can never write that column (PRD 8).

nodes.label: payment_events (table)
nodes.rationale: Unique (provider, provider_event_id) is what makes duplicate webhook delivery a no-op.

nodes.label: refund_requests (table)
nodes.rationale: A ticket workflow while refund policy is still pending owner approval; creating a request never moves money, it opens a case (PRD 7, 22).

nodes.label: invoices (table)
nodes.rationale: Invoice numbering is its own sequence, independent of orders; billing_snapshot freezes seller/buyer details as issued.

nodes.label: app.subscription_requires_verified_payment()
nodes.rationale: A subscription may only reach 'active' when a verified successful payment exists. Free plans (price 0) exempt. Enforced in the database, not merely respected by the app layer (PRD 8).

nodes.label: app.kot_requires_confirmed_order()
nodes.rationale: A KOT ticket may only exist for a CONFIRMED/IN_PROGRESS order, so an unpaid or unverified order cannot reach the kitchen at all.

nodes.label: payments_audit (trigger, redacts signature/raw payload)
nodes.rationale: Provider signatures and raw payloads are secrets-adjacent and are kept out of the audit trail (PRD 17).

nodes.label: coupons (table)
nodes.rationale: The 5% first-subscription offer is one row, not a constant: percentage, eligibility and lifetime are all editable. is_auto_visible shows an offer as already unlocked, but it still has to pass server validation (PRD 6, 14).

nodes.label: coupon_rules (table)
nodes.rationale: Eligibility predicates as rows so a new campaign shape needs no schema change.

nodes.label: coupon_redemptions (table)
nodes.rationale: Partial unique (coupon_id, subscription_id) means one subscription consumes a coupon exactly once, even under retry.

nodes.label: reviews (table)
nodes.rationale: Reviews start pending so nothing unmoderated ever renders publicly.

nodes.label: review_moderation (table)
nodes.rationale: Every status change is recorded, so hiding a review is itself auditable. No client write policy at all - moderation history is not something a browser token edits.

nodes.label: public.validate_coupon()
nodes.rationale: Server-side coupon validation: the browser may SHOW an offer as unlocked; only this decides whether it applies. 'First subscription' is checked against activated subscriptions, never inferred from the client.

nodes.label: notification_templates (table)
nodes.rationale: Message copy is data, not a deploy; nothing here assumes WhatsApp specifically (PRD 15).

nodes.label: notifications (table)
nodes.rationale: Doubles as the outbox: core flows enqueue inside their own transaction and return, so a failed send can never roll back an order or a payment. dedupe_key makes double-enqueue a no-op. to_address is snapshotted.

nodes.label: integration_accounts (table)
nodes.rationale: Credentials are NEVER stored - only the NAME of the secret to look up. Per-account breaker state (consecutive_failures, circuit_open_until) so one marketplace failing cannot stop the others (PRD 16).

nodes.label: integration_capabilities (table)
nodes.rationale: Per-feature honest state (integrated/mocked/blocked) with a reference_url; the UI reads this instead of implying capabilities we have not verified (PRD 16, 23).

nodes.label: integration_events (table)
nodes.rationale: Unique (provider, external_event_id) makes replayed marketplace webhooks idempotent.

nodes.label: integration_reconciliation (table)
nodes.rationale: Two-way reconciliation records the differences rather than silently trusting either side.

nodes.label: integration_accounts_audit (trigger, redacts credential refs)
nodes.rationale: Even the REFERENCE to a credential is kept out of the log.

nodes.label: public.quote_subscription()
nodes.rationale: The only place subscription pricing is computed. An invalid coupon is not an error - the caller gets a reason to show and the quote simply carries no discount. The browser never decides what anything costs (PRD 6, 8).

nodes.label: public.begin_subscription_checkout()
nodes.rationale: Creates a pending_payment subscription plus a pending payment and nothing else: it grants nothing, schedules nothing, produces no KOT. Idempotent on the checkout key; validates that the address belongs to the customer and that the plan offers the requested window.

nodes.label: app.assert_subscription_access()
nodes.rationale: SECURITY DEFINER RPCs bypass RLS, so each must prove for itself that the caller owns the subscription - otherwise passing someone else's id would be enough to pause their plan.

nodes.label: app.assert_customer_access()
nodes.rationale: Same guard for customer-scoped RPCs.

nodes.label: app.plan_cycle_credits()
nodes.rationale: Credit plans grant credits; meal-count plans grant one credit per meal and each meal consumes what its product says - so a premium meal costs more than one without a second code path.

nodes.label: app.base_priority()
nodes.rationale: Marketplace orders outrank scheduled subscription deliveries because they are immediate - and the numbers are a setting, not a constant (PRD 9).

nodes.label: public.confirm_subscription_payment()
nodes.rationale: The single door through which a subscription becomes real. Refuses outright if the provider signature was not verified. Idempotent: a duplicate webhook yields one activation, one credit grant, one invoice, one schedule.

nodes.label: public.fail_subscription_payment()
nodes.rationale: Leaves the subscription inactive and creates nothing downstream - no schedule, no ticket, no delivery. A late failure notice never undoes a confirmed payment; 'debited but unconfirmed' is its own reconciliation state, not a guess.

nodes.label: public.generate_subscription_deliveries()
nodes.rationale: Expands plan rules into dated rows; re-running an overlapping range is safe because the delivery unique key absorbs duplicates. meal_credits plans have no calendar and return 0.

nodes.label: public.schedule_credit_delivery()
nodes.rationale: Credit plans book against the ledger balance, checked on the server, never a cached number.

nodes.label: app.create_kot_ticket()
nodes.rationale: Allocates the daily source-prefixed number, base priority and SLA deadline. Returns the existing ticket if one exists - one ticket per order, always.

nodes.label: public.release_due_deliveries()
nodes.rationale: Turns scheduled deliveries into orders+tickets inside the configurable lead time. SKIP LOCKED makes it safe to run repeatedly and concurrently. Entitlement is checked against the ledger; insufficient credits BLOCK the release and are audited rather than silently released.

nodes.label: public.transition_kot_ticket()
nodes.rationale: All operational actions go through one door; the 0007 trigger decides legality and authorisation. Replaying the same transition is a no-op, because a double tap on a tablet under rush should not surface a failure. Keeps the order machine in step without either machine owning the other's columns.

nodes.label: public.override_prep_eta()
nodes.rationale: Manager-only; the original estimate is preserved so the override is visible in history rather than overwriting the kitchen's number (PRD 9).

nodes.label: public.skip_subscription_delivery()
nodes.rationale: Skipping returns entitlement as a compensating ledger entry, never an edit to the debit. Once a ticket exists the kitchen may be cooking, so skipping is no longer customer self-service.

nodes.label: public.pause_subscription()
nodes.rationale: Pause count and length are configurable and still pending owner sign-off; nothing hardcodes '2 pauses' or '3-5 days'. Deliveries inside the window are skipped by the same rule as a manual skip.

nodes.label: public.cancel_subscription()
nodes.rationale: Stops only future, not-yet-released deliveries; anything already in the kitchen stays in the kitchen. Historical and current-period record is preserved.

nodes.label: public.record_integration_failure()
nodes.rationale: Circuit breaker: health is tracked per account and read before any outbound call, so one marketplace failing never stops the others (PRD 16).

nodes.label: public.ingest_marketplace_order()
nodes.rationale: Idempotent on (source, external_order_id) AND on external_event_id: a replayed webhook returns the existing order instead of creating a second ticket. No payment row is created - marketplace orders are settled by the marketplace.

nodes.label: public.sync_marketplace_order_status()
nodes.rationale: Cancellation rules follow the marketplace, so a platform cancellation cancels our ticket even mid-preparation and says so in the history. A status for an order we never ingested is a recorded discrepancy, not an invented order.

nodes.label: public.reconcile_marketplace_orders()
nodes.rationale: Compares a window of external ids against what we hold and records differences; it never quietly creates or deletes anything.

nodes.label: v_kot_tickets (view)
nodes.rationale: The one board every operational screen reads. Money and contact columns are masked IN THE VIEW, so a reader without the permission gets nulls whatever they ask for - rather than trusting each caller to select the right columns (PRD 17).

nodes.label: v_kot_ticket_items (view)
nodes.rationale: What the kitchen actually cooks: names, quantities, variants, add-ons, instructions - prices masked the same way (PRD 5.4, 17).

nodes.label: v_customer_deliveries (view)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to app.current_customer_id() unless the reader holds subscriptions.view_all.

nodes.label: v_analytics_orders (view)
nodes.rationale: Subscription fulfilment orders contribute ZERO revenue here because website revenue is recognised on the subscription payment - counting both would double count.

nodes.label: v_revenue_by_source (view)
nodes.rationale: Website revenue from verified subscription payments; marketplace revenue from platform order totals.

nodes.label: v_kot_metrics_daily (view)
nodes.rationale: Revenue and cost are deliberately taken from different places and joined here: subscription revenue lands at payment verification while its cost lands on the fulfilment order days later. Summing order totals alone would show the website channel a permanent loss.

nodes.label: v_owner_dashboard (view)
nodes.rationale: Averages of daily averages are weighted by day, not by order - acceptable for a headline, with the per-day view there for detail.

nodes.label: v_integration_health (view)
nodes.rationale: Surfaces each capability's honest state plus breaker/reconciliation status for the Owner/Developer view (PRD 16).

nodes.label: app.guard_profile_privilege_columns()
nodes.rationale: A user may edit their own name and contact details but never their own role or is_active - that is the privilege-escalation path. A trigger, not a policy predicate, because a policy on auth_profiles that reads auth_profiles would recurse.

nodes.label: app.guard_review_status()
nodes.rationale: Only a moderator may change a review's status, and an edited review re-enters moderation rather than staying published.

nodes.label: auth_profiles_self_update (policy)
nodes.rationale: Scoped to the caller's own row; the privilege guard trigger is what stops role/is_active escalation within it.

nodes.label: audit_logs_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Readable only by Developer Admin and Owner; the append-only trigger stops anyone rewriting them (PRD 17).

nodes.label: business_settings_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Sensitive keys are invisible without settings.manage; the rest are public because fees and windows are shown on the storefront.

nodes.label: cost_settings_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Cost assumptions are commercially sensitive: staff who cannot see profit cannot see the inputs to it either.

nodes.label: products_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Unavailable products stay readable so the storefront can render them grayscale with a badge; unpublished and archived ones are not (PRD 19).

nodes.label: subscriptions_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Read-only by design: every subscription WRITE goes through the RPCs, so there is no client write policy at all.

nodes.label: orders_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Kitchen Staff deliberately do NOT hold orders.view - they work from the money-masking KOT views instead (PRD 5.4, 17).

nodes.label: kot_tickets_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Realtime for the operational screens rides on this policy; there is no client write policy, so a browser token cannot move a ticket by writing the column.

nodes.label: idempotency_keys_none (policy)
nodes.rationale: Idempotency records belong to the server; no client ever needs them.

nodes.label: coupons_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Only offers meant to be shown (active, auto-visible, in window) are visible without coupons.manage.

nodes.label: reviews_own_update (policy)
nodes.rationale: A customer may edit or withdraw their own review but cannot publish it; status changes belong to moderation.

nodes.label: integration_accounts_read (policy)
nodes.rationale: Credential REFERENCES are visible to integration managers only, and the credentials themselves never live in the database.

nodes.label: supabase_realtime (publication)
nodes.rationale: Realtime is the primary mechanism, not a polling fallback. Supabase applies the 0090 SELECT policies to every change event, so a Kitchen client receives ticket changes and nothing else. REPLICA IDENTITY FULL carries the previous row so clients can reconcile out-of-order or duplicated events rather than trusting arrival order.

nodes.label: Function EXECUTE deny-by-default
nodes.rationale: Supabase's broad default grants are fine for tables (RLS is the gate) but NOT for functions: several RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER. EXECUTE is revoked wholesale from public/anon/authenticated and granted back one function at a time, and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES keeps new objects in the same posture.

nodes.label: payment_provider 'sandbox' value
nodes.rationale: A non-production test gateway that signs its callback with HMAC-SHA256; confirm_subscription_payment still refuses to activate without a verified signature. It is not a bypass - what it does not do is move money, and the application refuses it when NODE_ENV is production.

nodes.label: app.handle_new_auth_user()
nodes.rationale: Without this a checkout signup has an auth.users row but no profile, so current_role() is null and every RLS policy denies them. New accounts are ALWAYS 'customer': self-service signup must never mint a privileged account.

nodes.label: app.handle_auth_user_updated()
nodes.rationale: Keeps contact details in step with Supabase Auth; role and is_active are deliberately untouched because those belong to the Owner, not the auth system.

nodes.label: on_auth_user_updated (trigger on auth.users)
nodes.rationale: Created conditionally: phone_confirmed_at exists on Supabase but not on a bare Postgres used for local testing.

nodes.label: app.review_set_verified_purchase()
nodes.rationale: The verified-purchase badge is only worth anything if the DATABASE decides it - a customer inserting through their own token could otherwise just set the column true. Trusted writers are exempt because they import history this query cannot see.

nodes.label: v_product_ratings (view)
nodes.rationale: Only published, undeleted reviews count, aggregated in the view rather than the page so the storefront cannot accidentally count a pending review.

nodes.label: public.moderate_review()
nodes.rationale: Annotates the review_moderation row the 0009 trigger just created rather than writing a second one, which would leave two competing records of one decision. A no-op decision leaves no trace, so history reads as decisions made rather than buttons pressed.

nodes.label: public.withdraw_refund_request()
nodes.rationale: Does the one thing a customer should be able to do, proving ownership first - rather than widening payments.manage, which would also let them edit a decision already recorded against them. An already-decided case is part of the record, not a draft.

nodes.label: auth_profiles_manage (policy)
nodes.rationale: Lets the Owner edit SOMEONE ELSE's profile; the 0090 privilege guard still stops anyone without employees.manage editing their own role.

nodes.label: customer_addresses_manage (policy)
nodes.rationale: An Owner-created customer has no login, so nobody but the Owner can give them an address. Kept as a permission-gated policy rather than service-role work so the write stays under RLS and the audit trigger keeps naming the real person.

nodes.label: Payment-Before-KOT Invariant
nodes.rationale: PAYMENT VERIFIED -> SUBSCRIPTION/ORDER CREATED -> KOT ELIGIBLE. PAYMENT FAILED -> NO ACTIVE SUBSCRIPTION -> NO KOT -> NO DELIVERY. Enforced by database triggers, not merely respected by the application layer.

nodes.label: Configuration as Data
nodes.rationale: Fees, taxes, delivery windows, grace periods, pause/skip rules, KOT lead time, base priorities and SLA minutes are rows read at request time. Retuning the business is an UPDATE, not a deploy (PRD 20).

nodes.label: Owner KOT Is Read-Only
nodes.rationale: The Owner holds kot.view but none of the kot.accept/start_prep/mark_ready/handoff/cancel permissions, so the transition trigger refuses their moves. Read-only is a row-level fact, not a UI decision (PRD 5.2, 9).

nodes.label: Append-Only History
nodes.rationale: Audit logs and the credit ledger are never updated or deleted; a correction is a new compensating row. Balance is always derived, so the history stays truthful.

nodes.label: Server-Authoritative Pricing
nodes.rationale: The browser asks for a quote, shows it, and submits a choice; the server recomputes the same numbers before any payment is created. Coupon eligibility, availability and address ownership are all re-decided server-side.

nodes.label: Snapshot Immutability
nodes.rationale: Names, prices, addresses, plan terms and billing details are frozen onto the record at the moment of the transaction, so later catalog or profile edits cannot rewrite what was sold or delivered (PRD 17).

nodes.label: Idempotency Everywhere
nodes.rationale: Every retryable boundary carries a uniqueness key: checkout keys, order idempotency_key, ledger (subscription_id, idempotency_key), delivery (subscription, date, window), payment provider_event_id and marketplace external_event_id. Replays are no-ops, not duplicates (PRD 7, 11).

nodes.label: Marketplace Failure Isolation
nodes.rationale: Health, consecutive failures and breaker state are per integration account, and capability state is declared honestly per feature, so one marketplace failing or lacking API access never stops the others (PRD 16, 23).

nodes.label: No Client Writes to Operational Tables
nodes.rationale: Orders, payments, subscriptions and KOT tickets have NO client write policy at all. Every mutation flows through SECURITY DEFINER RPCs that validate state, permission and idempotency first, so a compromised browser token cannot move a ticket or mint a subscription by writing a column.
nodes.norm_label: no client writes to operational tables

nodes.label: Cloud Kitchen Database Schema
nodes.rationale: Generated from supabase/migrations by scripts/build-bundle.mjs and never hand-edited, so the bundle and the migration history cannot drift. Every internal identifier is a UUID; human-facing numbers (order number, daily KOT number) are generated separately. Order state, payment state and KOT state are deliberately three independent lifecycles so an order can be CONFIRMED while its ticket is still NEW and a payment can be REFUNDED long after the order is COMPLETED.

nodes.label: Demo Seed Data
nodes.rationale: Seeds through the real schema and the real workflow functions rather than inserting into orders or kot_tickets directly, so a regressed invariant makes the seed itself fail. Runs with app.actor_id set to the Developer Admin so permission checks and the audit trail see a real actor. Ends with a self-check block asserting the PRD's core invariants.

nodes.label: auth_profiles table
nodes.rationale: One row per authenticated principal, keyed to Supabase auth; customers get a profile too with role = 'customer'. A trigger guards the privilege columns so a self-update cannot escalate role.

nodes.label: role_permissions table
nodes.rationale: Authorization is data, not code: which role may do what lives in this table so permissions can be retuned without a deploy.

nodes.label: employees table
nodes.rationale: Role quantities are data, never hardcoded: three kitchen accounts share one physical display, and a fourth hire is one more row.

nodes.label: audit_logs table
nodes.rationale: Append-only, enforced by an app.forbid_mutation trigger: nothing in the application can edit or delete an audit row. Readable only by Developer Admin and Owner via RLS.

nodes.label: business_settings table
nodes.rationale: Operational knobs (timezone, KOT release lead time, pause limits, COD enablement) live here so changing behaviour is a settings change, not a code change.

nodes.label: variant_groups table
nodes.rationale: Variant groups are defined once and shared across products rather than duplicated per dish.

nodes.label: customers table
nodes.rationale: Marketing consent is stored with its own timestamp, separate from account state, so disabling a login does not silently change consent and vice versa.

nodes.label: customer_addresses table
nodes.rationale: Addresses are retired via is_active rather than deleted: subscriptions and past deliveries point at these rows and a delivered order has to stay readable.

nodes.label: subscription_plans table
nodes.rationale: Four plan shapes exist as data (fixed_meals, meal_credits, scheduled_meals, customer_selected) so a new commercial shape is a row, not a branch in code.

nodes.label: subscription_plan_meals table
nodes.rationale: Fixed and scheduled plans define their own meals here; the customer-selected plan defines a selectable pool in the same table via is_selectable.

nodes.label: subscription_credit_ledger table
nodes.rationale: Append-only ledger, not a mutable balance column: the balance is always derived from entries, so a grant, a spend and a skip-refund each leave a permanent, auditable row.

nodes.label: subscription_deliveries table
nodes.rationale: Unique on (subscription_id, scheduled_date, delivery_window_id) so re-running generation over an overlapping range absorbs duplicates instead of double-booking.

nodes.label: orders table
nodes.rationale: Order state is kept deliberately separate from payment state and KOT state. Source prefixes SX (subscription), SW (Swiggy) and ZM (Zomato) make provenance readable on every order number.

nodes.label: kot_transitions table
nodes.rationale: The legal KOT state machine is stored as rows, so which transition is allowed from which state is retunable data rather than a hardcoded switch.

nodes.label: refund_requests table
nodes.rationale: Refund policy is not finalised, so the model records a case with a status rather than promising an automatic payout.

nodes.label: notifications table
nodes.rationale: Queued with next_attempt_at and a dead_letter terminal status, so a failing channel degrades into a retry queue instead of losing the message.

nodes.label: integration_capabilities table
nodes.rationale: Every marketplace feature is explicitly labelled integrated / mocked / blocked so the UI never implies more than the partner API really offers.

nodes.label: quote_subscription()
nodes.rationale: The single place subscription pricing is computed: subtotal, delivery fee, CGST/SGST split and whether a requested coupon actually applies. Centralising it means the storefront, checkout and invoice can never disagree about the price.

nodes.label: begin_subscription_checkout()
nodes.rationale: Creates a pending subscription and payment but schedules nothing and produces no KOT -- a subscription only becomes real once payment is verified. Idempotent on p_idempotency_key so a retried checkout returns the original subscription and payment instead of creating a second one.

nodes.label: confirm_subscription_payment()
nodes.rationale: The single door through which a subscription becomes real. Callable only by server-side code that has already verified the provider signature, and it refuses to proceed if p_signature_verified is false. Idempotent, so a duplicate webhook or a callback racing a webhook yields one activation, one credit grant, one invoice and one schedule.

nodes.label: fail_subscription_payment()
nodes.rationale: A failed payment must leave no active subscription and no KOT ticket; the seed asserts exactly this.

nodes.label: generate_subscription_deliveries()
nodes.rationale: Expands plan rules into dated delivery rows; re-running for an overlapping range is safe because the unique delivery key absorbs duplicates.

nodes.label: schedule_credit_delivery()
nodes.rationale: For credit plans the customer books a delivery against their balance, and the balance is checked here on the server against the ledger -- never trusted from the client.

nodes.label: release_due_deliveries()
nodes.rationale: Turns scheduled subscription deliveries into real orders and tickets only once they fall inside the configurable release lead time, so food enters the queue shortly before its window rather than days early. Safe to run repeatedly and concurrently: rows are locked with SKIP LOCKED and a released delivery is never picked up twice.

nodes.label: skip_subscription_delivery()
nodes.rationale: Skipping before the delivery reaches the kitchen returns the entitlement as a ledger credit, so the customer is never charged for food that was never cooked.

nodes.label: cancel_subscription()
nodes.rationale: Cancelling stops future deliveries but leaves already-released orders and all history intact.

nodes.label: validate_coupon()
nodes.rationale: Eligibility is decided server-side against coupon rules and prior redemptions; the storefront may advertise an offer as unlocked, but only this function decides whether it applies.

nodes.label: subscription_credit_balance()
nodes.rationale: Balance is derived by summing the append-only ledger rather than read from a stored counter that could drift.

nodes.label: ingest_marketplace_order()
nodes.rationale: Marketplace orders are settled by the marketplace, so no payment row is created; revenue is attributed from the totals the platform reports and reconciled later. Ingested tickets are indistinguishable from subscription tickets on the kitchen board.

nodes.label: reconcile_marketplace_orders()
nodes.rationale: Two-way reconciliation compares a window of external order ids against what we hold and records the differences; it never quietly creates or deletes anything.

nodes.label: withdraw_refund_request()
nodes.rationale: A customer may take a case back only before it has been decided; that rule lives in the function so the UI cannot loosen it.

nodes.label: app.has_permission()
nodes.rationale: Every RLS policy resolves through this helper, so permission logic exists once and is retuned by editing role_permissions rows.

nodes.label: app.audit_trigger()
nodes.rationale: Attached to every business table, so auditing is a property of the schema rather than something each code path must remember to do.

nodes.label: app.create_kot_ticket()
nodes.rationale: The one place a ticket is born, whether the order came from a subscription release or a marketplace ingestion -- which is why both sources land on the board identically.

nodes.label: app.kot_enforce_transition()
nodes.rationale: A trigger checks each status change against the kot_transitions whitelist, so an illegal jump is rejected however the update arrives -- UI, RPC or direct SQL.

nodes.label: app.setting() accessors
nodes.rationale: Typed accessors (setting_int, setting_bool, setting_numeric, setting_text) read business_settings so no operational number is hardcoded in a function body.

nodes.label: app.assert_customer_access()
nodes.rationale: Security-definer RPCs bypass RLS, so they re-assert ownership explicitly rather than assuming the policy already filtered the row.

nodes.label: app.subscription_requires_verified_payment()
nodes.rationale: A trigger-level invariant: a subscription cannot reach active without a verified payment, so no code path can activate one by accident.

nodes.label: app.kot_requires_confirmed_order()
nodes.rationale: No ticket may exist for an unconfirmed order: the kitchen never cooks food that was not paid for or accepted.

nodes.label: app.review_record_moderation()
nodes.rationale: Editing a published review sends it back to pending from a database trigger, so the rule holds however the edit arrives rather than depending on the account page.

nodes.label: app.guard_profile_privilege_columns()
nodes.rationale: auth_profiles allows a self-update policy, so a trigger blocks changes to role and is_active to stop a customer promoting themselves.

nodes.label: RLS as the Authorization Boundary
nodes.rationale: Every page query runs under the caller's own token, so Row Level Security -- not a WHERE clause in a page file -- is what confines a customer to their own rows and a staff member to their permitted ones. Consequence: an unauthorised session sees an empty table rather than a leak, and forgetting a filter in a new page cannot become a data breach.

nodes.label: Authorization Is Data, Not Code
nodes.rationale: Which role may do what lives in role_permissions rows resolved by app.has_permission, so permissions can be retuned without a deploy. The same principle covers role headcount, plan shapes and KOT transitions: quantities and rules are rows, never constants.

nodes.label: Append-Only History
nodes.rationale: audit_logs and subscription_credit_ledger are protected by forbid_mutation triggers. Protects the ability to answer 'what happened and who did it' after the fact, and makes a derived balance trustworthy because nothing can retroactively rewrite the entries it sums.

nodes.label: Verified-Payment Gate
nodes.rationale: Checkout creates intent only; a subscription becomes real solely through confirm_subscription_payment with a verified provider signature, and a trigger independently refuses an active subscription without one. Protects against a spoofed callback, a client-side 'success' redirect, or a race between webhook and callback creating food the kitchen was never paid for.

nodes.label: Idempotent Money Paths
nodes.rationale: Checkout keys on an idempotency key, confirmation is idempotent, delivery generation absorbs duplicates on a unique key, and release locks rows SKIP LOCKED. Protects against double-charging, duplicate schedules and double-released tickets under retries and concurrency.

nodes.label: Derived Balance Over Stored Counter
nodes.rationale: Meal-credit balance is always computed from the ledger. Protects against drift between a cached counter and reality when a skip refunds a credit or a premium dish costs two.

nodes.label: Seed Through Real Workflows
nodes.rationale: Demo data is produced by calling the same functions the app calls instead of inserting frontend-only fake arrays, so the seed doubles as an end-to-end invariant test: if a rule regresses, the seed fails to run.

nodes.label: Subscription-Only Commerce
nodes.rationale: Menu and Meal Plans are browsing and education surfaces with deliberately no standalone meal checkout; Subscriptions is the only place a purchase begins. Knowing the day's demand before it starts is what keeps a single-kitchen operation viable.

nodes.label: Retire, Never Delete
nodes.rationale: Addresses are deactivated, reviews get a deleted_at, products get archived_at. Subscriptions and delivered orders point at these rows, and a delivered order has to stay readable; business records a food business must keep survive account closure.

nodes.label: Replace the Whole Relationship Set
nodes.rationale: Collections, variant groups and add-ons each submit their complete set and the action deletes then reinserts. A partial update would leave a dish attached to a collection the Owner had just unticked -- exactly the quiet divergence the storefront would then render.

nodes.label: Availability-First Kitchen Controls
nodes.rationale: Marking a dish unavailable is the most frequent catalog action in a kitchen -- something runs out and the storefront must stop offering it within seconds -- so it is one click on the list screen with a customer-visible reason, while everything else about a dish lives in the per-dish editor.

nodes.label: Storefront Shell Layout
nodes.rationale: Navigation is fixed to Home, Menu, Meal Plans, Subscriptions, Offers, About. Mobile uses a scrollable row rather than a hidden menu so every destination stays one tap away.

nodes.label: About Page
nodes.rationale: States the data-retention posture in plain language: business records persist after account closure, and marketing consent is a separate switch from account state.

nodes.label: Menu Page
nodes.rationale: Shows unavailable dishes greyed out with the reason instead of hiding them, so a customer sees an honest kitchen state rather than a silently shrinking menu.

nodes.label: Meal Plans Page
nodes.rationale: Education, not commerce: it explains how the food is grouped and how a week looks; the purchase happens on Subscriptions.

nodes.label: Offers Page
nodes.rationale: Advertises offers but states that eligibility is checked at order time and the reason will be given at checkout, rather than failing quietly.

nodes.label: Subscriptions Listing Page
nodes.rationale: Translates the four plan-type enums into plain-language explainers and states up front that skip, pause and cancel exist -- the commitments the backend actually implements.

nodes.label: continueToCheckout server action
nodes.rationale: Deliberately stores intent only, validated by draftSchema. No subscription, no payment and no price exists until checkout runs begin_subscription_checkout on the server; a rejected configuration redirects back with ?error=invalid and nothing is charged.

nodes.label: Customer Account Layout
nodes.rationale: Guards the session once for every account page, but each page still resolves its own customer record: a signed-in staff member has a session and no customer row, and should be told so rather than shown an empty dashboard.

nodes.label: Account Addresses Page
nodes.rationale: Every query and write runs under the customer's own token, so RLS confines them to their own addresses -- not a filter in this file.

nodes.label: makeDefaultAddress server action
nodes.rationale: Clears is_default across the customer's addresses before setting the new one, so exactly one default can exist.

nodes.label: retireAddress server action
nodes.rationale: Sets is_active false rather than deleting, because subscriptions and delivered orders still point at the row.

nodes.label: Account Refund Requests Page
nodes.rationale: Refund policy is still being finalised, so the page raises a case and says so plainly rather than implying a guarantee the business has not agreed to.

nodes.label: Account Reviews Page
nodes.rationale: Reviewable dishes are the ones actually delivered, resolved from subscription_deliveries and their items; RLS already confines both queries to this customer so neither filters by customer itself.

nodes.label: updateReview server action
nodes.rationale: Does not itself reset moderation status; the reviews_record_moderation trigger sends an edited published review back for checking, so the rule holds however the edit arrives.

nodes.label: Admin Audit Log Page
nodes.rationale: Readable only by Developer Admin and Owner, enforced by RLS rather than by this page, which is why an unauthorised session sees an empty table instead of a leak. The log is append-only in the database: nothing here can edit it.

nodes.label: toggleAvailability server action
nodes.rationale: One-click, with a reason captured, and it revalidates /menu immediately so the storefront stops offering a sold-out dish within seconds.

nodes.label: Admin Product Editor Page
nodes.rationale: One dish end to end -- name, description, images, category, collections, price, variants, add-ons, calories, availability and special instructions -- none of it hardcoded anywhere else.

nodes.label: setArchived server action
nodes.rationale: Archives via archived_at instead of deleting, keeping historical order items and reviews resolvable.

nodes.label: addImage / makePrimaryImage actions
nodes.rationale: Clears is_primary across the dish's images before setting one, so a product can never show two primary images.

nodes.label: POST /api/checkout/begin
nodes.rationale: Session-guarded checkout entry. Re-validates the chosen payment provider against configuredPaymentProviders() because the client is not the authority on which gateways have credentials; a draft that has expired is refused before any customer or payment row is created.

nodes.label: POST /api/checkout/confirm
nodes.rationale: Before verifying a gateway callback it re-reads the payments row joined to customers.profile_id and requires it to equal session.id. Without that ownership check a signed-in customer could post a callback against someone else's payment id. The draft is only cleared when the outcome is 'active'.

nodes.label: POST /api/checkout/sandbox
nodes.rationale: Stands in for a gateway hosted page. The signing key never leaves the server, so a browser cannot mint a callback; it signs an outcome only for the caller's own sandbox payment, then routes it through the same verifyCallback path and confirm_subscription_payment checks a real provider uses. Signing and verifying in one process makes the crypto circular here, but it still proves that an unverified outcome activates nothing, a declined outcome creates no subscription and no KOT, and retries are idempotent.

nodes.label: POST /api/kot/transition
nodes.rationale: Deliberately does not decide whether a ticket move is legal. It calls transition_kot_ticket with the caller's own token so the database trigger checks both transition legality and the actor's permission. An Owner's token still cannot accept a ticket -- read-only KOT is enforced in the database, not by hiding a button. Trigger errors mentioning 'may not perform transition' or 'insufficient' are mapped to 403 rather than 500.

nodes.label: POST /api/kot/eta
nodes.rationale: Manager-only ETA override; the route does not check the permission itself, override_prep_eta re-checks it, and any RPC error is returned as 403.

nodes.label: POST|GET /api/jobs/notifications
nodes.rationale: Drains the notification outbox (PRD 15). Kept separate from the flows that enqueue messages so a provider outage delays notifications and nothing else -- no order, payment or ticket depends on this endpoint succeeding. GET aliases POST because hosted cron runners issue GET; safe only because the work is idempotent.

nodes.label: POST|GET /api/jobs/reconcile
nodes.rationale: Two-way marketplace reconciliation over a rolling 24h window (PRD 16). It records differences and never creates or deletes an order to make numbers agree -- a discrepancy is a finding for a human. Swiggy and Zomato are handled in independent try blocks so one failing provider does not stop the other.

nodes.label: POST|GET /api/jobs/release-deliveries
nodes.rationale: Releases scheduled subscription deliveries into the active KOT (PRD 7, 9). All the decision logic is in release_due_deliveries, which reads the configurable lead time, locks rows with SKIP LOCKED and is idempotent, so overlapping runs are safe and a missed run catches up next time.

nodes.label: Admin Shell Layout
nodes.rationale: Gate is requireAnyPermission([analyticsView, catalogManage, auditView]). The SECTIONS nav is filtered by session.permissions so a role is not shown a link into a wall -- explicitly a courtesy, not the security boundary: each page guards itself and RLS guards the data underneath.

nodes.label: Admin Loading Skeleton
nodes.rationale: Skeleton shape mirrors the heading-then-rows layout of admin pages so content does not jump on arrival.

nodes.label: Admin Business Overview
nodes.rationale: Guarded by analytics.view. Reads v_owner_dashboard and v_kot_metrics_daily; cross-source averages are weighted by order count so a quiet channel does not drag the headline. Checks cost_settings.is_dummy_data and warns that profit is only as good as placeholder cost inputs while revenue and timings are real (PRD 12, PRD 22).

nodes.label: Admin Variant Groups
nodes.rationale: Guarded by catalog.manage (PRD 13). A group is defined once and attached to many dishes; each option carries its own price, credit and calorie delta so a larger portion legitimately costing an extra credit is data, not an assumption baked into checkout.

nodes.label: Admin Offers and Coupons
nodes.rationale: Guarded by coupons.manage (PRD 14). Every coupon behaviour -- percentage, caps, window, eligibility rules -- is a row, so the 5% first-subscription offer can be retuned or retired without a deploy. Dates are anchored to Asia/Kolkata (PRD 10) so 'valid until 31 March' does not expire at 05:30 on a UTC deployment. Eligibility is still decided server-side by validate_coupon() at checkout; this screen only authors the rules. A redeemed coupon is not deletable because deleting it would erase a discount someone actually received.

nodes.label: Admin Customers List
nodes.rationale: Guarded by customers.view or customers.manage; write forms are gated on can(session, customersManage). The manual create form exists for phone orders, walk-ins and migrated records, which is why customers.profile_id is nullable -- such a customer has business records but no login. Search input is sanitised before it reaches a PostgREST `or` filter because commas and parentheses can break out of the filter.

nodes.label: Admin Customer Detail
nodes.rationale: Guarded by customers.view or customers.manage (PRD 14). Deactivation is never a hard delete: it disables the auth_profiles login while orders, invoices and payments stay intact, and it deliberately leaves marketing consent alone because consent is not a function of account status. Only one address may be default (a partial unique index enforces it) so the old default is stood down first; subscriptions reference addresses with ON DELETE RESTRICT so retiring is the only safe removal.

nodes.label: Admin Employees
nodes.rationale: Guarded by employees.view or employees.manage (PRD 5). Role quantities are rows not constants, and what a role may do lives in role_permissions, so this screen assigns a role and never a permission. Only session.role === 'developer_admin' may assign developer_admin -- the Owner runs the business and does not hand out system access. Creating the login is the single step needing the service key (no user exists yet to hold a token); everything after runs on the Owner's token so RLS and the audit trigger apply and name them rather than 'system'. If role assignment fails the just-created login is torn down. The current role is re-read from the database rather than trusted from the form so 'unchanged' cannot be asserted into a promotion, and employees/auth_profiles are kept in agreement so a badge never disagrees with permissions.

nodes.label: Admin Integration Health
nodes.rationale: Guarded by integrations.view (PRD 16, PRD 23). The screen exists for honesty: every capability is labelled integrated, mocked or blocked straight from integration_capabilities so nobody can come away believing Swiggy or Zomato are connected when they are not.

nodes.label: Admin Subscription Plans
nodes.rationale: Guarded by plans.manage (PRD 7, PRD 13). Creation asks only for the commercial minimum so step one is not forty fields; a new plan is never published until its menu and windows exist. Plans are archived, never deleted, because live subscribers reference them, and archiving also unpublishes so a 'deleted' plan cannot keep selling.

nodes.label: Admin Plan Editor
nodes.rationale: Guarded by plans.manage (PRD 7, PRD 13). Three separate forms -- commercial terms, rule overrides, menu -- so saving a price does not resubmit the menu and adjusting a pause limit cannot blank a delivery window. Null overrides mean 'inherit the global setting', genuinely different from zero. Windows are replaced wholesale rather than diffed because the form always submits the complete set and a partial update would leave a plan sellable in a window the Owner just unticked. Editing a plan never rewrites what an existing customer bought -- purchases carry a frozen plan_snapshot (migration 0006).

nodes.label: Admin Refund Requests
nodes.rationale: Guarded by payments.view or payments.manage (PRD 7, PRD 22). Refund policy is still pending owner sign-off, so this is deliberately a case workflow, not a refund button: recording a decision moves no money and touches no payment. Terminal statuses stamp resolved_at.

nodes.label: Admin Review Moderation
nodes.rationale: Guarded by reviews.moderate (PRD 14). Reviews arrive pending and never render publicly until published, and that ordering is enforced by RLS rather than by this screen. Moderation goes through moderate_review, which writes a review_moderation row naming the moderator, so hiding a review is itself part of the audit history. Revalidates /menu as well as the admin path.

nodes.label: Admin Business Settings
nodes.rationale: Guarded by settings.manage (PRD 20). This screen is the proof that nothing business-critical is hardcoded: grace period, pause limits, KOT release lead time, tax rates, delivery fee and cost assumptions are all rows that take effect on the next request with no deploy. Values stored as jsonb must survive the round trip -- a number written as a string would break setting_int at read time -- so an input that cannot round-trip is refused with a reason rather than silently swallowed. Unconfirmed values are marked provisional (PRD 22). RLS re-checks settings.manage on write.

nodes.label: getSession()
nodes.rationale: Refuses an inactive auth_profile, which is what actually stops a deactivated employee or customer signing in.

nodes.label: can(session, permission)
nodes.rationale: Used to hide or disable write controls on read-only admin screens; the real enforcement is RLS underneath.

nodes.label: confirmCheckout()
nodes.rationale: Single funnel for every provider callback: verifies the gateway signature then applies confirm_subscription_payment, so activation cannot be reached by any other path.

nodes.label: clearDraft()
nodes.rationale: Only called once an outcome reports status 'active', so a failed or uncertain payment leaves the customer's plan selection intact for a retry.

nodes.label: adminClient() (service-role Supabase)
nodes.rationale: Bypasses RLS, so it is used only where no caller token could exist or suffice: job endpoints, cross-customer payment ownership lookups, and creating an auth user for a brand-new employee.

nodes.label: serverClient() (caller-token Supabase)
nodes.rationale: Carries the caller's own JWT so RLS policies, permission triggers and audit attribution all apply to admin reads and writes.

nodes.label: isAuthorisedJob(request)
nodes.rationale: Bearer-secret gate shared by every scheduled job route; there is no session on a cron request, so this is the only authentication those endpoints have.

nodes.label: marketplaceAdapter(provider)
nodes.rationale: Returns an adapter whose listOrderIds may answer not-ok with a reason and state, which the reconcile job records as 'skipped' rather than treating as agreement.

nodes.label: Admin action feedback (done/fail/readable)
nodes.rationale: Turns a Postgres constraint or RLS error into a sentence the Owner can act on, and redirects back with a status so a failed server action is never silent.

nodes.label: transition_kot_ticket() RPC
nodes.rationale: Holder of the KOT state machine: a trigger checks both that the from/to transition is legal and that the calling actor holds the permission that transition requires. Raises 'may not perform transition' / insufficient_privilege, which the route translates to 403.

nodes.label: override_prep_eta() RPC
nodes.rationale: Re-checks the manager permission itself rather than trusting the calling route.

nodes.label: release_due_deliveries() RPC
nodes.rationale: Decides what is due from the configurable lead time, locks with SKIP LOCKED and is idempotent, so overlapping cron runs are safe.

nodes.label: reconcile_marketplace_orders() RPC
nodes.rationale: Compares an external id list against internal orders for a window and records missing_internal / missing_external counts as a finding; it does not mutate orders.

nodes.label: moderate_review() RPC
nodes.rationale: Applies the review status change and writes a review_moderation row naming the moderator, so moderation is auditable.

nodes.label: confirm_subscription_payment() RPC
nodes.rationale: Database-level end of the payment state machine: applies the same checks for sandbox and real providers, so an unverified outcome activates nothing, a declined outcome creates no subscription and no KOT, and a retry is idempotent.

nodes.label: validate_coupon() RPC
nodes.rationale: Coupon eligibility is decided server-side at checkout; the admin coupons screen only authors the rules it reads.

nodes.label: developer_admin role
nodes.rationale: Only an existing developer_admin may assign developer_admin; the Owner runs the business but does not hand out system-level access.

nodes.label: customers table
nodes.rationale: profile_id is nullable so a phone-order or migrated customer can hold business records with no login.

nodes.label: auth_profiles table
nodes.rationale: Holds role and is_active; deactivating the profile is what actually blocks sign-in, since getSession() refuses an inactive profile.

nodes.label: role_permissions table
nodes.rationale: What each role may do is data, not code, which is why the employees screen assigns a role and never a permission.

nodes.label: customer_addresses table
nodes.rationale: A partial unique index allows only one default per customer, and subscriptions reference addresses ON DELETE RESTRICT so retiring is the only safe removal.

nodes.label: reviews table
nodes.rationale: Reviews arrive pending and RLS, not the admin screen, is what keeps an unpublished review off the public menu.

nodes.label: business_settings table
nodes.rationale: jsonb key/value store for grace period, pause limits and KOT release lead time; types must round-trip or setting_int breaks at read time.

nodes.label: cost_settings table
nodes.rationale: Carries is_dummy_data so the dashboard can label profit as an estimate rather than presenting placeholder assumptions as settled policy.

nodes.label: Defense-in-depth authorization
nodes.rationale: Three independent layers: the nav hides links a role cannot use (courtesy only), each page calls requirePermission/requireAnyPermission, and RLS plus permission triggers guard the data. No layer is trusted to be the only one -- an Owner's token reaching an endpoint directly is still refused by the database.

nodes.label: Server-side payment provider allowlist
nodes.rationale: A provider without credentials is never offered in the UI and is refused again server-side, because the client is not the authority on what is available.

nodes.label: Payment ownership check
nodes.rationale: Every callback endpoint re-reads the payment joined to customers.profile_id and requires it to match session.id, otherwise a signed-in customer could post a callback against someone else's payment id. A mismatch returns 404 rather than 403 so payment ids are not confirmable by probing.

nodes.label: KOT state machine enforced in the database
nodes.rationale: The API route validates shape only. Legality of a from/to move and the actor's permission to make it are both decided by the transition trigger under the caller's own token, so a hidden button is never the control -- an Owner's read-only KOT holds even against a direct API call.
nodes.norm_label: kot state machine enforced in the database

nodes.label: Idempotent cron endpoints behind a bearer secret
nodes.rationale: Job routes have no session, so isAuthorisedJob's bearer secret is their only authentication. GET is aliased to POST because hosted schedulers issue GET, which is acceptable only because each job's work is idempotent -- overlapping or missed runs are safe.
nodes.norm_label: idempotent cron endpoints behind a bearer secret

nodes.label: No hardcoded business policy
nodes.rationale: Grace periods, pause and skip limits, KOT release lead time, tax and delivery rates, cost assumptions, coupon percentages, variant price deltas and role permissions are all rows the Owner edits, effective on the next request with no deploy.

nodes.label: Archive, never hard delete
nodes.rationale: Customers are deactivated, plans archived (and unpublished so they stop selling), addresses retired, and redeemed coupons kept -- because the orders, invoices, payments and discounts behind them are legitimate business records.

nodes.label: Reconciliation reports, never repairs
nodes.rationale: The job records missing_internal / missing_external counts and never creates or deletes an order to make totals agree; a discrepancy is a finding for a human, not something to paper over.

nodes.label: Honest integration and estimate labelling
nodes.rationale: Mocked or blocked marketplace capabilities, placeholder cost assumptions and unconfirmed settings are labelled as such (PRD 22/23) so no screen lets a reader believe something is live or settled when it is not.

nodes.label: Service key only where no caller token can exist
nodes.rationale: Creating an employee login needs the service key because no user exists yet to hold a token; every subsequent step runs on the Owner's token so RLS and the audit trigger apply and name the real actor. If the role grant fails, the orphan login is deleted rather than left usable.
nodes.norm_label: service key only where no caller token can exist

nodes.label: Frozen plan snapshot
nodes.rationale: A purchase carries a plan_snapshot (migration 0006), so editing a plan's price, menu or windows never retroactively rewrites what an existing subscriber bought.

nodes.label: Marketplace Webhook Route (Swiggy/Zomato)
nodes.rationale: Ordered as raw-body -> verify -> idempotent RPC because parsing first would change the bytes the signature was computed over, and an unverified payload must never be ingested as a real order. Rejected payloads are still written to integration_events so a misconfigured or hostile sender is visible to the Owner rather than silently dropped. Unknown providers 404 and each provider's failure only trips its own breaker, so one marketplace outage cannot take down the other or the website.

nodes.label: Payment Provider Webhook Route
nodes.rationale: The webhook, not the browser callback, is the authoritative confirmation path because it arrives even if the customer closes the tab mid-payment. An unmatched payment returns HTTP 200 rather than an error so the provider does not retry something that can never be matched; it is recorded for reconciliation instead. Both callback and webhook converge on the idempotent confirm_subscription_payment, so a race produces one activation, one credit grant and one invoice.

nodes.label: Checkout Page
nodes.rationale: Step is derived from session state (no session -> auth, no customer -> profile, no address -> address, else payment) rather than stored, so a refresh or a returning customer lands on the correct step. Every price shown comes from the server-side quote_subscription RPC and is recomputed by begin_subscription_checkout before a payment is created, so what the browser believes the price is never matters. A failed profile or address insert is surfaced loudly because a silent refusal would strand the customer on a step that never advances.

nodes.label: Route Error Boundary
nodes.rationale: Offers a real retry because most failures here are transient database or network calls that reloading genuinely fixes, and it never implies the underlying action succeeded -- if a form threw on the way to the server the customer must know the work did not land. The raw message is withheld from the user; only the digest is shown, because that is what ties this screen to the server log entry.

nodes.label: Forbidden Page
nodes.rationale: Says plainly that the role does not cover the screen instead of pretending the page does not exist, because staff following an internal link deserve a straight answer. It embeds a sign-out control because otherwise someone signed in under the wrong role has no exit except clearing cookies by hand.

nodes.label: Global Error Boundary
nodes.rationale: Last-resort boundary for a failure in the root layout itself. It supplies its own html/body and deliberately depends on nothing -- no fonts, no design tokens, no shared primitives -- because whatever broke may be one of those; all styling is inline literals.

nodes.label: Not Found Page
nodes.rationale: Serves both bad URLs and anything a page resolves with notFound() -- a retired plan slug, an archived dish, a customer id that was never real -- so it offers onward routes (home, menu, plans) rather than only an apology.

nodes.label: Root Layout
nodes.rationale: Holds the font variables, global stylesheet and the title template ('%s · Cloud Kitchen') that every page's metadata slots into.

nodes.label: Kitchen Display Page
nodes.rationale: Filters v_kot_tickets to KITCHEN_STATUSES only: the kitchen sees accepted work onward, because whether to accept a ticket is the manager's commercial decision, not the kitchen's (PRD 9). It passes no money or customer commercial data to the board. force-dynamic because a cached render would be a stale board.

nodes.label: KOT Manager Page
nodes.rationale: Shows ACTIVE_STATUSES (the wider set including unaccepted tickets) and computes canAct from PERMISSIONS.kotAccept rather than from the role name. The Owner holds kot.view and not kot.accept, which is precisely what makes the Owner's board read-only while the Manager's is actionable. Server-renders the first paint then hands over to the realtime socket, so the screen is useful before JavaScript settles on a kitchen tablet.

nodes.label: Sign In Page
nodes.rationale: Redirects an already-signed-in user to landingPathForRole so staff and customers never sit on a sign-in form they do not need. force-dynamic because the demo panel reads live account rows; listDemoAccounts returns null unless SHOW_DEMO_ACCOUNTS is set, in which case the accounts are never even queried.

nodes.label: Account Nav
nodes.rationale: Addresses, reviews and refunds get their own tabs rather than living under the overview so none of them is buried beneath a subscription the visitor may not have yet. '/account' matches exactly because it is a prefix of every other tab.

nodes.label: Subscription Controls (Pause / Cancel)
nodes.rationale: Neither pause nor cancel fires on a single click: pausing demands dates, cancelling demands explicit confirmation and states that deliveries already with the kitchen will still be prepared. Pause/cancel limits are enforced server-side from settings, so this form deliberately does not restate them as client rules -- it only reports whatever the server says when a request is refused.

nodes.label: Admin Nav
nodes.rationale: Client component purely so the current section can be highlighted; with eleven destinations 'where am I' is not obvious from the heading. The sections array is already permission-filtered on the server -- this component never decides what anyone may reach, so hiding a link is presentation, not authorization.

nodes.label: Catalog Nav
nodes.rationale: Products are the daily work; categories, collections, variant groups and add-ons are the scaffolding a product is assembled from, kept on separate screens so the product editor can stay about one dish. /admin/catalog/products/... still highlights the Products tab.

nodes.label: Revenue Chart
nodes.rationale: Hand-rolled inline SVG rather than a charting library because this is one chart of fixed shape and shipping a plotting runtime to draw twenty rectangles costs more than it returns. Channel colours follow the PRD source coding, but the legend also carries the literal SX/SW/ZM prefix so colour is never the only indicator (PRD 19); each bar segment carries a <title> for hover and screen readers.

nodes.label: Demo Accounts Panel
nodes.rationale: 'Use' fills the form rather than making you copy two fields, because the real job is checking each role quickly. Clipboard access can be denied or absent over plain HTTP, so every copy falls back to window.prompt text selection instead of showing a 'Copied' that never happened. Renders only while SHOW_DEMO_ACCOUNTS=true.

nodes.label: Sign In Form
