hyperedges.description: No single pair captures it: the payments check constraint, the activation trigger, the ticket-insert trigger and the release path together guarantee that unverified money never reaches the kitchen.

hyperedges.label: Cross-boundary idempotency mesh
hyperedges.description: Seven independent unique keys spanning four migrations implement one invariant: any retry, webhook replay or concurrent confirmation produces exactly one activation, one grant, one order and one ticket.

hyperedges.label: Authorization-as-data resolution path
hyperedges.description: Every RLS policy and every KOT move resolves through the same chain of rows and helpers, which is why 'Owner may watch but not touch the KOT' is a data fact rather than a code branch.

hyperedges.label: Scheduled delivery released into a live kitchen ticket
Catalog edit propagating to the storefront
Payment verification and activation chain
hyperedges.rationale: Every route into activation passes the same four gates in order: session, payment ownership against customers.profile_id, gateway signature verification in confirmCheckout, then confirm_subscription_payment in the database. Only an 'active' outcome clears the draft. The sandbox route joins the chain at the same point a real gateway would, which is what makes it an end-to-end proof that an unverified or declined outcome creates no subscription and no KOT and that retries are idempotent.

hyperedges.label: KOT transition authorization chain
hyperedges.rationale: Both KOT write endpoints validate only the request shape, then call an RPC with the caller's own token. Legality of the move and the actor's permission (data in role_permissions) are decided by the database trigger, so an Owner's read-only KOT survives a direct API call and 'insufficient privilege' surfaces as 403.

hyperedges.label: Scheduled job layer
hyperedges.rationale: Three cron endpoints share one shape: bearer-secret authentication (no session exists), the service-role client, idempotent work, and GET aliased to POST for hosted schedulers. Each is isolated so a failure degrades one concern only -- a notification provider outage blocks no order, and a failing marketplace does not stop the other being reconciled.

hyperedges.label: Marketplace webhook ingestion path
hyperedges.note: One inbound request traverses all six: raw body read, signature verified (rejections logged to integration_events), idempotent ingestion into a KOT ticket, and on failure a provider-scoped breaker trip.

hyperedges.label: Payment confirmation and activation path
hyperedges.note: Checkout prices server-side and creates the payment; the webhook dedupes on the provider event id, matches the internal payment, and confirms it exactly once regardless of whether the browser callback also arrived.

hyperedges.label: Sign-in journey
hyperedges.note: Page redirects the already-authenticated by role, panel owns the credential state the demo table fills, form authenticates without revealing which emails exist, and the forbidden screen closes the loop by offering sign-out as the way back for a wrong-role session.

hyperedges.label: The shared button family
hyperedges.rationale: One class builder feeds three renderings that differ only in semantics: Button (does something, knows about a pending form via useFormStatus), ButtonLink (goes somewhere, a real <a> so tab order and open-in-new-tab work), ConfirmButton (does something destructive, composing Button twice to get arm-then-confirm). Spinner is the shared in-flight affordance for all of them.

hyperedges.label: Realtime KOT board sync and honesty
hyperedges.rationale: Both boards subscribe through useKotBoard and mutate through useTicketActions; ConnectionBadge exposes the subscription's real state so a silently stalled board is never mistaken for a live one, and TicketItems fetches lines per ticket so the realtime firehose stays cheap. The kitchen sees a money-free, large-type subset of the same ticket stream the manager acts on.

hyperedges.label: Idempotent, verified checkout
hyperedges.rationale: One key minted at configuration time travels in the draft cookie into begin_subscription_checkout, which replays instead of duplicating; the service then reuses any existing gateway order for that payment. Nothing is granted until confirmCheckout gets a verified signature, and the UI turns the three server outcomes into three honest screens including the unconfirmed one.

hyperedges.label: One PaymentAdapter contract, three gateways, one resolver
hyperedges.rationale: All three adapters absorb their gateway's idiosyncrasies (paise vs rupees, order id vs session token, HMAC vs re-query) so checkout code is identical, and all three obey the same two rules: verify on the server, never mutate application state. paymentAdapter() refuses an unconfigured adapter and configuredPaymentProviders() decides what is even offered, so a customer can never begin a checkout against a gateway that would fail.

hyperedges.label: Constant-time HMAC verification across every trust boundary
hyperedges.rationale: Every inbound trust boundary -- payment webhook, payment callback, marketplace webhook, cron header -- uses the same shape: recompute an HMAC-SHA256 over the RAW body (parsing first would break the signature), length-check, then timingSafeEqual. The signed material and encoding differ per provider (order|payment hex for Razorpay and sandbox, raw body hex for Razorpay webhooks and the marketplaces, timestamp+body base64 for Cashfree), but a missing secret or header is always a rejection, never a pass-through.

hyperedges.label: Realtime as signal: refetch, resync, and the DB wiring that backs it
hyperedges.rationale: The board never trusts a change payload as data -- only as a row id to refetch from v_kot_tickets -- which makes duplicate and out-of-order events idempotent and keeps the view's money-masking in force. Gaps are closed by full resync on reconnect, network-online and tab-visible, never by an interval. The anon browser client means RLS filters which events arrive at all, and the realtime test asserts the publication and the single SELECT policy that make both properties true at the database.

hyperedges.label: The Four-Role RBAC Model
hyperedges.rationale: Four staff roles whose boundaries are defined as role_permissions rows rather than code, each role's screen shaped by what it may not see: Owner watches without touching, Manager runs the floor without pricing, Kitchen cooks without money, Developer Admin configures everything but cannot rewrite history.

hyperedges.label: The Payment Safety Guarantee
hyperedges.rationale: Together these mean no food is cooked and no entitlement granted without a server-verified payment, retries cannot double-charge, uncertain outcomes are reconciled rather than guessed, and a fake gateway is unreachable in production.

hyperedges.label: The Honest-State Doctrine
hyperedges.rationale: One idea expressed at every layer: never display, imply or persist a state the system has not actually reached — no optimistic lies, no invented endpoints, no unvalidated number passing as decided, no silently swallowed refusal.
